Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that cytokines play a significant role in epilepsy. Specifically, studies suggest that increased post-ictal (after an epileptic seizure) serum cytokine levels are associated with several epilepsy syndromes.

Cytokines are proteins released by immune cells that help fight off infections and inflammation. In the context of epilepsy, cytokines may play a role in the inflammatory processes that occur during seizures, potentially contributing to their development or severity.
